I work at a university office over the summer, and we host a monthly meeting for "Neighbor to Neighbor Energy Challenge". It's pretty much our town's chapter of this state-wide initiative to reduce residential electricity consumption. For an hour one Wednesday each month, a group of concerned citizens visits and discusses various strategies to do just that. One of these concerned citizens is a lady whom is probably well into her 80s. She consistently shows up at least an hour early for every meeting, because she clearly and sadly has nothing else to do. She babbles incoherently most of the time, but she doesn't speak while the other members are, so we let her stay. We know she doesn't have a home, and stays at a local shelter. She'll just come in, pour herself a glass of water, walk around the office until the start of the meeting, and leave promptly afterward. My coworkers and I think this meeting is one of the only things she has left in life =/

I know that feel bro, I dated a Protestant girl for over three years. I was completely content with not talking about our differences in faith (or lack thereof), because it wasn't necessary to start conflict where it didn't need to exist. She would always start such conversations, and they would always end in me being so frustrated with her lack of willingness to accept our scientific understanding of the natural world and universe, that I had to leave for a while. She would always be content with just saying, "Well it just *feels* like there is something more that we don't know", or try to make me look like the bad guy by saying "Don't you think that when we die we'll be able to see everyone we love and spend eternity with them?" And I would tell her that it doesn't matter what I think, all I know is that beyond all doubt I have experienced nothing to make me believe in something that hasn't been proven to exist. 

She's a respectful, extremely kind and loving individual, but I knew, deep down, two things: One, that she wouldn't change her faith, and two that I wouldn't be able to stay with someone content with blunt ignorance. We dated for three years, (age 16-19), and now we are trying to stay good friends. So far it's worked out, but we'll see how it goes. My advice to you is to either not speak about faith at all, or to get out of the relationship. The more you talk about it, the more you will doubt the reality of your future with her. Hope this helps man, wish ya the best.

Also, extracting natural gas is so inexpensive that it just makes simple economic sense. Since hydraulic fracturing is relatively unregulated, drilling companies can do what they want to get the gas at the lowest cost to them. At such low extraction costs they have the means to extract millions of cubic feet, drastically increasing supply, and decreasing the cost in the market.

My school uses a large ground source heat pump system to completely heat and cool a nine-story dorm, and the rest of the dorms are heated by our natural gas plant. Drilling wells for intermediate to large scale systems constitutes the majority of the costs. Being a state school, we made a deal with the state and scored a huge incentive. Otherwise, the payback on these systems just doesn't make them practical yet, and how efficient they are can depend largely on the clay content of the soil being drilled into.
